title: timed-fair-slot-reshaper: reduce tail latency and starvation in continuous batcher
author: Miguel Santos
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching has reduced unit cost but occasional tail spikes and starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests persist under mixed workloads. This PR introduces a timed fair slot reshaper that dynamically reshapes admission windows to preserve fairness while maintaining high aggregation efficiency.

Summary of changes: Adds a timed-slot reshaper that sits between the admission queue and the batch coalescer. The reshaper keeps soft time windows per logical lane and tracks recent slot consumption to bias upcoming time slices toward starved lanes. It introduces a starvation sentinel that will preempt a small portion of a batch when a lane's historical wait exceeds a threshold, and a short randomized soft-timeout jitter to avoid synchronization under bursty arrivals. The reshaper emits metrics that let the console detect if the reshaper is actively rebalancing slots (reshaper.active_pct) and lane-level wait quantiles. Additionally, the reshaper exposes a lightweight hint interface for the KV cache layer so prefetch hints can be applied when a request is admitted but delayed to the next slot — this reduces cold-kv misses for starved lanes. The feature is designed to be opt-in via runtime config flags and to fall back to existing behaviour when disabled.

Design notes: - Timed-slot windows are sized relative to target latency SLOs and request size histograms. Small/interactive lanes get smaller windows with higher reshaping priority. - Starvation sentinel counts per-lane wait time and uses an exponential backoff to avoid oscillation. - Prefetch hinting: when a request is deferred to the next slot, we call KV prefetch_hint(keyset) asynchronously; prefetch path is lockfree and best-effort. - Kernel hint handshake: reshaper emits an inline hint that the kernel selection layer can use to favor lower-latency kernels for lanes marked interactive (heuristic only).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR: ENG-3421 design notes included in description - [x] Unit tests for reshaper logic and starvation sentinel - [x] Microbench perf harness (mixed small+large reqs) - [x] Integration test with kv cache hint path - [x] Metrics, logs, and docs - [x] Rollout plan with feature flag and staged percentage - [x] Non-blocking rollback via feature flag

Testing & results: Microbench (locally) with 10k qps mixed workload (80% small interactive, 20% large generation) shows 95th latency of small requests reduced from ~220ms to ~140ms and 99th reduced from ~560ms to ~310ms. Throughput drop under full aggregation was <2% when feature enabled. CI perf job initially flagged a small regression in a large-model continuous batcher integration test; that was due to an overly-aggressive default window cap — adjusted defaults and re-ran CI.

Rollout: Default state is disabled. Deploy stage: (1) Enable on low-traffic cluster with reshaper metrics monitored; (2) Ramp to 10% routes; (3) Ramp to 50%; (4) Global on. Backout via feature flag toggles immediately reverts to previous behaviour.

Risks and mitigations: - Overly aggressive reshaping can reduce batch efficiencies: mitigated by conservative default caps and runtime tuning via console. - KV prefetch hints could increase transient memory usage: prefetch is best-effort and bounded per-lane. - Kernel hint is advisory only and will not change kernel selection unless explicit opt-in is set in model config.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative change surface: core admission path is unchanged when disabled, and all new bookkeeping is kept lockfree where feasible. Full design doc and tuning guidance included in docs/ops/reshaper.md.

release_notes: Introduce timed fair slot reshaper to reduce tail latency for small/interactive lanes. Opt-in via feature flag; default disabled. Includes KV prefetch hint integration and metrics for reshaping activity.
notes_for_oncall: If reshaper.active_pct spikes and latency for large requests increases >10% persistently, toggle feature off via reshaper_toggle flag and notify SRE. Prefetch failures are logged as debug and are best-effort; no immediate action unless memory pressure metrics rise.
